sentences.text:
Re  Mr. P.Mishra, 
 CORAM:
 JUSTICE B. P. ROUTRAY  ORDER 16.08.2023 Order No.
07. 1.
The matter is taken up through Hybrid mode.

2. Heard Mr. Roy, learned counsel for the Appellant and Mr.Mishra, learned counsel for the Respondents.
3. Present appeal by the Insurer is directed against judgment dated 18th December, 2021 of 1st MACT, Puri in M.A.C. Case No.136 of 2013, wherein compensation to the tune of Rs.11,34,897/- has been granted along with interest @7% per annum with effect from the date of filing of the claim application on account of death of the deceased in the motor vehicular accident on 1st June, 2012.
4. Mr.Roy submits that the deceased initially filed the claim application as an injured and he subsequently died on 21st May 2016, i.e. near about four years after the date of accident.

He further Manager vs Binati Sahoo & Ors on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199779477/
1 submits that in absence of any connection between the death of the deceased with the injury sustained in the accident, Location: High Court of Orissa, Cuttack the Claimants are not entitled for any compensation under the provisions of MV Act.
5. The accident took place on 1st June 2012.
The involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident and sustenance of injuries on the part of the deceased due to the accident is not disputed.
It is the consistent case of the Claimants that the deceased sustained 75% disability in the accident and was under continuous treatment till the date of this death.

The injury report reveals sustenance of brain injury by the injured due to the accident the medical report also substantiate the continuous treatment of the injured due to such brain injury at different hospitals.

On the other hand, no evidence has been adduced from the side of the Insurer and no rebuttal material could be produced by the Insurer against the claim of the applicants regarding death of the deceased out of brain injury.

Therefore, all such contentions raised by Mr.Roy are rejected being without merit and it is held that the death of deceased is due to such injuries sustained in the accident involving the offending vehicle.
6. The Tribunal has granted Rs.5,80,800/- towards loss of dependency and added medical expenses of Rs.5,01,297/- thereon to determine the compensation amount at Rs.11,34,897/-.
Such computation of compensation amount appears erroneous.
At this stage Mr.Roy submits that the grant of medical expenses to the tune of Rs.5,01,297/- is not supported by material evidence.
Further, the monthly income of the deceased has been taken at Rs.6,000/- without any income proof.
Location: High Court of Orissa, Cuttack 7.

Dealing with the submission made by Mr.Roy regarding medical expenses, the same is found without any merit particularly when the admitted fact remains that the deceased was under continuous medical treatment for a period of four years having sustained brain injury.
8. So far as the income of the deceased is concerned, the Tribunal has accepted him as a daily labourer and fixed his income at Rs.6,000/- per month in the year 2012.
9. As per the prevalent minimum wage rate, it was Rs.90/- per day for unskilled labourer till 30th September 2012 and increased to Rs.150/- with effect from 1st October 2012.
The enhanced rate of minimum wage was notified in Notification No. 1942 dated 6th October 2012.

Since the date of accident is 1st June 2012, which is just four months prior to the date of enhancement, in the circumstances, the income of the deceased on the date of accident is accepted at Rs.4,000/- per month by way of guess work.
It needs to be mentioned here that the Tribunal has accepted the deceased as a daily labourer in absence of any proof towards his income.
Said part of the findings of the Tribunal is never challenged by the Claimants.

Adding future prospects to the extent of 10%
thereto and deducting 1/3rd towards personal expenses, the annual loss of dependency comes to Rs.35,200/-.
Applying multiplier 11, the total loss of dependency becomes Rs.3,87,200/-.
Adding Rs.1,00,000/- towards general damages including consortium to the widow and both sons, the amount comes to Rs.4,87,200/-.

Location: High Court of Orissa, Cuttack 10.
Therefore, the total compensation amount is determined of Rs.9,88,497/- payable along with interest @6%.

11. In the result, the appeal is disposed of with a direction to the Insurer-Appellant to deposit the modified compensation of Rs.9,88,497/- (Nine lakhs eightyeight thousand four hundred ninty seven) along with interest @ 6% per annum with effect from the date of filing of the claim application within a period of two months from today; where-after the same shall be disbursed in favour of the Claimants No. 1, 2 & 3 on such terms and proportion to be fixed by the Tribunal.
However, penal interest @ 8% as directed by the Tribunal is waived.

12. The statutory deposit made by the Appellant with accrued interest thereon shall be refunded to him on proper application and on production of proof of deposit of the award amount before the learned Tribunal.
13. Urgent certified copy of this order be granted on proper application.
